breast MRI is a useful tool for the detection of occult breast cancer and for determining the extent of disease in patients with newly detected breast cancer.
breast MRI is useful in women with a newly diagnosed invasive breast cancer, particularly for those with a high risk for mammographically undetected disease.

breast MRI should be considered in patients with newly detected breast cancer to assess for additional disease, particularly in patients at high risk for contralateral disease and those with axillary nodality.

the impact of breast MRI on the management and outcomes of patients with newly diagnosed cancer.
the development of a novel and innovative approach to the development of a new cancer.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
breast MRI is an effective and useful adjunct to the evaluation of the patient with newly detected breast cancer.

breast MRI is indicated to evaluate patients with a newly discovered breast cancer, and that the use of breast MRI is associated with a reduction in the rate of reoperation for positive margins and a reduction in the number of patients who require a mastectomy.

breast MRI is a valuable tool for patients with recently diagnosed breast cancer and should be performed in a practice with a dedicated breast MRI radiologist and technologist and a facility with the ability to perform breast MRI-guided biopsy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

MRI has a high sensitivity for detecting additional breast cancers in the affected and the contralateral breasts in patients with a newly discovered cancer, and that the use of breast MRI may be considered to evaluate the extent and location of ipsilateral disease, screen the contralaterl breast, and identify the primary malignancies in patients with axillary adenocarcinomas.

the current NCCN breast MRI guidelines are based on published research, and that the use of MRI in patients with a newly diagnosis breast cancer should be limited to practice sites that have demonstrated the ability to perform high-quality breast MRI.

the use of breast MRI for patients with newly diagnosed cancer has been demonstrated to be safe and beneficial, but the quality of breast MR images and the quality of the interpretation of the images vary greatly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
breast MRI is an important tool for the patient with newly-diagnosed breast cancer.
breast MRI is an important tool for the patient with newly detected breast cancer and that the use of MRI in this setting is associated with a high degree of patient satisfaction.

breast MRI should be considered for patients at increased risk for occult cancer and for those with a known breast cancer to evaluate for the presence of additional cancer in the ipsilateral and contralateral breast.
